title: Cross-model tokenflow and prefetching heuristics
content:
Objective:
Notes from exploratory profiling focused on token movement ("tokenflow") and prefetching heuristics for long-context workloads across Llama / Mistral / Qwen and hybrid MoE variants. Goal is to capture observable differences in when prefetch wins/loses, how routing affects memory access patterns, and practical runtime knobs that reduce p95 for 32k+ contexts.

Summary of findings (top-level):
- Models with wider per-layer KV footprints (eg. Llama pa 8k->64k tests) benefit from early, coarse-grained prefetch of KV blocks; however, aggressive prefetch (fetch N future blocks) increases tail latency under bursty arrival patterns because it competes for GPU PCIe/CPU-to-GPU bandwidth with concurrent batch transfers.
- Mistral-like layouts (smaller per-token tape but more layers) show higher sensitivity to kernel invocation overhead; prefetching needs to target batching of contiguous sequence ranges rather than many small non-contiguous KV requests.
- Qwen's attention tiling (observed on our quantized variants) reduces memory reads per-token but increases compute kernel launch cost; lightweight prefetch (prefetch only when seq_len growth > threshold) works best.
- MoE routing interacts poorly with naive prefetch: routing decisions cause unpredictable expert KV touches. Best approach for MoE is two-stage prefetch: 1) prefix-level coarse prefetch for gating probabilities above threshold, 2) on-demand expert KV prefetch with per-expert LRU window.

Environment & tools used:
- Hardware: p4d.24xlarge (A100-80GB) and internal 8xH100 (80GB) test bench.
- Profilers: NVIDIA Nsight Systems (nsys), nvtx ranges instrumented in runtime, CUPTI sampling for memory copy breakdowns.
- Runtime build: branch tokenflow-prefetch-experiments @ commit 3a9b7f (local patch set attached in PR 1987).
- Test harness: synthetic generator to produce mixed short/long-context queries with inter-arrival jitter modeled on production traces (sampled from prod-route-analytics 2025-10).

Key experimental setups (short):
1) Baseline: no prefetch, standard KV cache fetch on demand. Measure p50/p95 p99 for single-request latency across sequence lengths [2k,8k,32k,64k], batching disabled.
2) Aggressive prefetch: prefetch next 8 KV blocks when sequence grows.
3) Adaptive prefetch: prefetch when sequence growth rate (tokens/sec) > threshold and estimated remaining length > window.
4) MoE gating-aware: prefetch candidate experts with gating prob >0.2; do per-expert NVMe->GPU staged copy with small concurrency cap.

Representative numbers (A100, single request):
- Llama-64k baseline: p50=980ms, p95=1.45s, p99=2.1s
- Llama-64k aggressive prefetch: p50=970ms, p95=1.6s, p99=3.3s (worse tail) -- explanation: prefetch created PCIe contention and blocking of on-demand KV for concurrent small bursts.
- Llama-64k adaptive prefetch: p50=975ms, p95=1.38s, p99=1.9s (best overall)
- Mistral-32k baseline: p50=420ms, p95=650ms
- Mistral-32k batched-prefetch (contiguous windows): p50=410ms, p95=540ms (good improvement)
- Qwen-32k quantized baseline: p50=500ms, p95=780ms; prefetched on growth-only: p95 down to 630ms.
- MoE-32k (8 experts hot): baseline p95=1.2s; naive prefetch p95=1.9s; gating-aware two-stage p95=1.05s.

Observations and micro-behavior:
- NVLINK/PCIe stage: on machines where NVME->GPU staging had to go via PCIe, prefetching can monopolize DMA engines and stall smaller urgent transfers. Nsight traces show long memcopy ranges overlapping with tiny kernel launches, leading to increased queueing latency.
- Kernel launch vs memcpy: Mistral's many small linear layers increase ratio of kernel launches to memcpy cost; grouping prefetches into fewer, larger contiguous transfers reduces relative overhead.
- KV cache hotness: long-running sessions show large skew in KV access (prefix tokens dominate). For models with long prefix reuse (chat sessions), prefix caching + server-side pinned pages significantly reduces remote prefetch need.
- MoE gating variability: expert selection entropy increases with long context because routing input distribution drifts; prefetch based on previous-step gates underestimates future touches. We found using short lookahead (2–4 tokens) with probabilistic thresholds gave good tradeoff.

Heuristics that worked well in practice (implementation notes):
- AdaptivePrefetchV1: only enable prefetch when (estimated_remaining_tokens >= 0.6 * max_context) AND (average_token_arrival_rate > R). R tuned per-tier: 40 tokens/s for interactive, 200 tokens/s for streaming batch.
- ContiguousWindowTransfers: detect if next K requested KV blocks are contiguous on storage layout; merge into single DMA when contiguous. K default 4, tunable per model.
- ExpertPrefetchBudget: per-request cap on how many experts can be prefetched (default 3). Maintain per-expert in-flight counter to avoid saturating PCIe.
- PrefetchBackoff: exponential backoff on prefetch if observed memcopy latency > T ms (T derived from baseline percentiles).

Runtime knobs added (config names):
- prefetch.enabled (bool)
- prefetch.mode = [off|aggressive|adaptive|moe-gated]
- prefetch.window_kv_blocks (int)
- prefetch.contiguous_merge (bool)
- prefetch.per_expert_cap (int)
- prefetch.memcopy_latency_threshold_ms (int)
- prefetch.arrival_rate_threshold (float)
Note: these knobs have been instrumented with runtime metrics (prefetch_attempts, prefetch_aborts, prefetch_memcopy_ms) and surfaced in the console route-level dashboard.

Problems encountered and open questions:
- Measuring true cause of p99 regressions is noisy; on shared testbeds background replication I/O sometimes spikes memcopy times. Need re-run on isolated host or dedicated NIC.
- How to get robust gating lookahead? Tried LSTM-based gating predictor trained on sampled routing traces; reduced mis-prefetch by 15% but added compute & model complexity. Worth it? Might be overkill; simpler short-window heuristic OK for now.
- Interaction with quantization: quantized weights reduce memory transfer size but increase compute time slightly; optimal prefetch window shrinks. Need an auto-tuning pass per-model-version.
- Edge case: prefetching when request is near the end of context leads to waste. We rely on estimated_remaining_tokens but estimation errors persist when clients truncate. Consider explicit client hint headers ("expected_remaining") in API.

Short checklist for follow-ups and experiments:
- [ ] Re-run Llama-64k adaptive prefetch on dedicated host to confirm tail improvement reproducibility. (Assigned: Diego)
- [ ] Implement contiguous-merge detection in storage layout layer (Lin).
- [ ] Collect routing entropy per-session for MoE to calibrate expert_prefetch_budget (Sophie).
- [ ] Add telemetry for PCIe DMA occupancy and GPU copy queue lengths (priority: high).
- [ ] Run automated sweep across quantization profiles to find prefetch window per qconfig.

Suggested short-term path to shipable behavior:
1) Default prefetch.mode=adaptive with conservative thresholds (windows_kv_blocks=2, arrival_rate_threshold=40 tokens/s).
2) Enable contiguous_merge by default for models with contiguous storage layouts (Mistral variants).
3) Expose per-route prefetch tuning in console with recommended presets (interactive/streaming/batch).
4) For MoE, ship gating-aware prefetch but keep default per_expert_cap=2; expose per-customer toggle due to workload variance.

Notes-to-self (fragments):
- Trace snippets show memcopy overlap: see NVTX ranges labeled PFETCH_* around 0x7f9a3.. that eat into KERNEL_* launches. Add guard to pause PFETCH when kernel queue depth crosses X.
- Consider moving some small expert KV slices into device-side cache pool for very hot experts to avoid repeated staging (cost vs memory tradeoff).
- Client hints experiment: add optional header X-Expected-Remaining and see if model servers can reduce waste by 40–60% in some chats.

References and links:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1987 (implementation + microbench harness)
- Linear: RED-3421 tokenflow prefetch experiments
- Confluence draft: PROF-Tokenflow-Playbook (internal draft)

If we want to move forward: prioritize telemetry (DMA occupancy + per-prefetch memcopy ms) + dedicated re-runs for Llama-64k. After that, iterate on adaptive thresholds and add a lightweight predictor for MoE gating (rule-based first, ML fallback later).

End of notes.
